title: Fix StringRegister byte order: Serial ID and Device name swapped within each 16-bit word
description: StringRegisters read from the device have their bytes swapped within each 16-bit Modbus register. Serial ID (5001) shows HQ2248RHJUF instead of HQ2248RHJUFm; Device name (5027) shows VESCH-2Q42R8JHFU instead of EVCS-HQ2248RHJUF. The fix is to use little-endian byte order per word when decoding read values, and correspondingly swap bytes when writing. Affects read path in cli.py (read_registers) and write path (write_register).
close_reason: Fixed: > to < in struct.pack/unpack for StringRegister read and write paths

title: Create tui.py: Textual register editor app
description:
New file tui.py implementing a full-screen Textual app with:
- DataTable (6 cols: Address, Name, Value, Unit, Default, Access); R-only rows dimmed
- Arrow key navigation; Enter to begin/confirm edit on R/W rows (no-op on R); Escape to cancel and restore
- Pending writes tracked with * prefix; Ctrl+S writes all pending (stops on first failure, shows error in status bar)
- Ctrl+R refresh with confirmation dialog if pending writes exist
- Ctrl+Q quit with Yes/No/Cancel confirmation dialog if pending writes exist
- Footer bar showing key bindings and pending count
- 10 async Pilot tests in tests/test_tui.py
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-14-write-tui-design.md § TUI

title: Add validate_write_value and write_register to reader.py
description:
Add two functions to reader.py:
- validate_write_value(reg, input_str): parse human-readable display value, apply scale conversion (float * scale → round → int), validate type bounds (uint16: 0-65535, int16: -32768-32767), raise ValueError on invalid input. Returns raw int for scalar, str for StringRegister.
- write_register(client, reg, value): FC6 for scalar (int16 wire encoding: value+=65536 if <0), FC16 for StringRegister (UTF-8 encode, null-pad to register_count*2 bytes, big-endian uint16 words). Catches all exceptions, returns bool.
Add 9 reader tests covering both functions. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-14-write-tui-design.md § Reader Changes

title: Write confirmation: read back register after write to verify change
description: After writing a register via FC6 or FC16, perform a read-back (FC3) to confirm the device accepted the new value. If the read-back value does not match what was written, report a warning. Useful for detecting device-side range rejection or read-only overrides.

title: Notes column: show spec description text in table and TUI

Display in a dedicated column in the reader table and TUI so users understand what each register does without consulting the spec sheet. Consider truncation or a detail panel for long notes.

title: Range validation against spec-defined min/max values
description: When writing register values, validate against the spec-defined range (e.g. Charging current: 6-32, Charge mode: 0-2) rather than just the type bounds (uint16: 0-65535). Requires parsing the 'Range' column from the spec sheet and adding a range: tuple[int, int] | None field to Register.
